label: Life expectancy at age 60
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = UN DYB Tables 21/22 (life expectancy at specified ages, by sex), national life tables as reported by each country, 13 editions 2011-2015 + 2017-2024, sex-split as printed (Male/Female rows, no both-sexes column to report). Witness tier = WHO GHO WHOSIS_000015 (WPP-derived modeled estimates, 183 countries, 2000-2021; the uncertainty intervals are carried nowhere — dropped at parse, re-fetchable from source_url).
license: Mixed, per source (see "sources"): UN DYB = UN data reuse policy (attribution required, no endorsement implied); GHO witness = CC-BY-3.0-IGO.
notes:
THE COMPANION INDICATOR (Extra board): LE at birth answers "how long is a life"; LE at 60 answers "how long is old age" — the Todd-relevant distinction for any reading of aging societies. The two indicators share the DYB's sex discipline (Male/Female printed separately; no both-sexes column, and averaging would be a derivation), so every canonical point carries sex="male"|"female" and (entity, year, sex) is the merge key.
THE RENUMBERING ZONE: "Life expectancy at specified ages" swaps table numbers with the 5qx probabilities by edition parity (verified across all 13 wired editions): table 21 in even editions, table 22 in odd ones. A number-only dispatch would silently mis-parse the 5qx file (identical layout) — the connector's title guard keys on the title's WORDS and raises with the parity rule if the config asks for the wrong number.
CROSS-SECTION SEMANTICS (the structural difference with the other indicators): each edition prints each country's LATEST available life table only. The canonical series is therefore a stack of cross-sections across the 13 editions, not an annual panel: a country that stops responding freezes (Russia's last life table is 2012 — repeated identically in every edition 2013-2024, merged into ONE point), and a country responding annually contributes one newer year per edition. Read the gaps between points as "no newer life table was available", never as missing years of an annual series.
REFERENCE PERIODS: a block's year row can be a single year ("2019") or an explicit period ("2012 - 2015", "2022 - 2024"). The point's year is the END of the printed period — the DYB's own convention, verified edition by edition against Table 4 (France 2015 + Roman IV = period 2012-2015 appears in Tables 4 and 22 of the 2017 edition as the same life table; same for Mauritius 2017/III, Dominican Republic 2015/VI). The printed period rides the points' reference_range. Three countries print actuarial-style multi-year tables extending beyond the edition year (Dominican Republic / Philippines / Yemen "2020 - 2025" in the 2024 edition): kept as printed, year = 2025, the collector republished the country's own submitted period.
THE 2024 DUAL BLOCK: France carries TWO blocks in the 2024 edition — the full 2020 life table and a 2024 block where only age 0 is published (ages 5-100 print "..."). The 2024 block materializes as an explicit gap for LE-60: the collector's own not-yet-computed degradation, kept as-printed, exactly like Table 15's "counts published, no rate".
NO QUALITY CODES, NO MARKER CELLS: like Table 4, this table prints no C/U/| code (that legend describes registration completeness, not life tables) and no markers next to the values; the BIFF editions glue footnote references to the country names and to the YEAR rows ("20103" = 2010 + note 3 — the split is deterministic, DYB years are always 4 digits); both ride the points' footnote_refs.
WITNESS TIER: who_gho WHOSIS_000015 "Life expectancy at age 60" — WPP-derived modeled estimates (not registrations), 2000-2021, three sex series (male / female / both). The canonical/witness spread is the displayable signal: Russia 2012 male = 15.38 as-reported vs 15.43 modeled; France 2020 male = 22.77 vs 22.60. The witness's uncertainty intervals (Low/High in the API payload) are carried by neither tier: dropped at parse (the raw snapshots hold parsed records only), re-fetchable from source_url — adding them to the dist is a schema decision to take explicitly if the frontend ever needs them.
